name: steppingStoneFst
docstring:
**Stepping-stone Fst model.**
    In the stepping-stone model, migration occurs only between adjacent demes.
    Fst between demes separated by d steps is approximately:
    Fst(d) ≈ Fst_neighbor × (1 + α × (d - 1))
    where α controls the rate of increase with distance (isolation by distance).
    This is a linear approximation to the closed-form result.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def steppingStoneFst (fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  fst_neighbor * (1 + α * ((d : ℝ) - 1))

name: steppingStoneFst_at_one
docstring: Stepping-stone Fst at distance 1 equals the neighbor Fst.
proof:
by
  unfold steppingStoneFst
  simp
raw:
theorem steppingStoneFst_at_one (fst_neighbor α : ℝ) :
    steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α 1 = fst_neighbor := by
  unfold steppingStoneFst
  simp

name: steppingStoneFst_increases_with_distance
docstring:
**Stepping-stone Fst increases with geographic distance** (isolation by distance).
    For positive neighbor Fst and positive distance scaling parameter α,
    Fst is strictly increasing in the number of steps.
signature:
(fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d₁ d₂ : ℕ)
    (hfst : 0 < fst_neighbor) (hα : 0 < α) (hd : d₁ < d₂)
body: steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d₁ < steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d₂
proof:
by
  unfold steppingStoneFst
  have hd_real : (d₁ : ℝ) < (d₂ : ℝ) := Nat.cast_lt.mpr hd
  have h_inner : α * ((d₁ : ℝ) - 1) < α * ((d₂ : ℝ) - 1) := by nlinarith
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem steppingStoneFst_increases_with_distance
    (fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d₁ d₂ : ℕ)
    (hfst : 0 < fst_neighbor) (hα : 0 < α) (hd : d₁ < d₂) :
    steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d₁ < steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d₂ := by
  unfold steppingStoneFst
  have hd_real : (d₁ : ℝ) < (d₂ : ℝ) := Nat.cast_lt.mpr hd
  have h_inner : α * ((d₁ : ℝ) - 1) < α * ((d₂ : ℝ) - 1) := by nlinarith
  nlinarith

name: steppingStoneFst_neighbor_lt_distant
docstring:
**Nearby demes have lower Fst than distant demes.**
    Fst(1) < Fst(d) for d > 1 under the stepping-stone model.
signature:
(fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d : ℕ)
    (hfst : 0 < fst_neighbor) (hα : 0 < α) (hd : 1 < d)
body: steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α 1 < steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d
proof:
by
  exact steppingStoneFst_increases_with_distance fst_neighbor α 1 d hfst hα hd
raw:
theorem steppingStoneFst_neighbor_lt_distant
    (fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d : ℕ)
    (hfst : 0 < fst_neighbor) (hα : 0 < α) (hd : 1 < d) :
    steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α 1 < steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d := by
  exact steppingStoneFst_increases_with_distance fst_neighbor α 1 d hfst hα hd

name: steppingStoneFst_nonneg
docstring: **Stepping-stone Fst is nonneg for valid parameters.**
signature:
(fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d : ℕ)
    (hfst : 0 < fst_neighbor) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
proof:
by
  unfold steppingStoneFst
  apply mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hfst)
  have : 0 ≤ α * ((d : ℝ) - 1) := by
    apply mul_nonneg hα
    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) := Nat.one_le_cast.mpr hd
    linarith
  linarith
raw:
theorem steppingStoneFst_nonneg (fst_neighbor α : ℝ) (d : ℕ)
    (hfst : 0 < fst_neighbor) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    0 ≤ steppingStoneFst fst_neighbor α d := by
  unfold steppingStoneFst
  apply mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hfst)
  have : 0 ≤ α * ((d : ℝ) - 1) := by
    apply mul_nonneg hα
    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) := Nat.one_le_cast.mpr hd
    linarith
  linarith

name: sharedLD_from_equilibrium
docstring:
**Shared LD derived from Fst equilibrium.**
    Defined as `1 - fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m`, i.e., the complement
    of the between-population divergence under migration-drift balance.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def sharedLD_from_equilibrium (Ne m : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 - fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m

name: sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq
docstring:
The shared LD fraction derived from Fst equilibrium equals M/(1+M).
    This is the formal derivation: starting from Fst = 1/(1+M), we obtain
    shared_LD = 1 - 1/(1+M) = M/(1+M).
body: sharedLD_from_equilibrium Ne m = scaledMigrationRate Ne m / (1 + scaledMigrationRate Ne m)
proof:
by
  unfold sharedLD_from_equilibrium fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium scaledMigrationRate
  have hden : 1 + 4 * Ne * m ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring
raw:
theorem sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq (Ne m : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    sharedLD_from_equilibrium Ne m = scaledMigrationRate Ne m / (1 + scaledMigrationRate Ne m) := by
  unfold sharedLD_from_equilibrium fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium scaledMigrationRate
  have hden : 1 + 4 * Ne * m ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring

name: sharedLDFromMigration
docstring:
**Shared LD fraction under migration-drift balance.**
    Gene flow homogenizes LD patterns between populations. The fraction of LD
    that is shared between two demes increases with migration rate:
    shared_LD(m) = M / (1 + M) where M = 4Nm.

    **Derivation:** This formula is the complement of the Wright (1931)
    island-model Fst equilibrium. Since Fst = 1/(1+M) (proved at
    `fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium`), the shared fraction is
    1 - Fst = 1 - 1/(1+M) = M/(1+M). See `sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq`
    and `sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq_sharedLDFromMigration` for the
    formal algebraic derivation.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def sharedLDFromMigration (M : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  M / (1 + M)

name: sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq_sharedLDFromMigration
docstring:
The derived shared LD fraction equals `sharedLDFromMigration M`. This
    closes the loop: the formula M/(1+M) is not an assumption but follows
    from the migration-drift Fst equilibrium.
body: sharedLD_from_equilibrium Ne m = sharedLDFromMigration (scaledMigrationRate Ne m)
proof:
by
  rw [sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq Ne m hNe hm]
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  rfl
raw:
theorem sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq_sharedLDFromMigration (Ne m : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    sharedLD_from_equilibrium Ne m = sharedLDFromMigration (scaledMigrationRate Ne m) := by
  rw [sharedLD_from_equilibrium_eq Ne m hNe hm]
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  rfl

name: sharedLDFromMigration_nonneg
docstring: Shared LD fraction is nonneg for nonneg M.
proof:
by
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  exact div_nonneg hM (by linarith)
raw:
theorem sharedLDFromMigration_nonneg (M : ℝ) (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
    0 ≤ sharedLDFromMigration M := by
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  exact div_nonneg hM (by linarith)

name: sharedLDFromMigration_lt_one
docstring: Shared LD fraction is at most 1.
proof:
by
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  rw [div_lt_one (by linarith : 0 < 1 + M)]
  linarith
raw:
theorem sharedLDFromMigration_lt_one (M : ℝ) (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
    sharedLDFromMigration M < 1 := by
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  rw [div_lt_one (by linarith : 0 < 1 + M)]
  linarith

name: sharedLDFromMigration_increases
docstring:
**Shared LD fraction increases with migration rate.**
    More migration → more shared LD → better PGS portability.
signature:
(M₁ M₂ : ℝ)
    (hM₁ : 0 < M₁) (_hM₂ : 0 < M₂) (h_more : M₁ < M₂)
proof:
by
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by linarith)]
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem sharedLDFromMigration_increases (M₁ M₂ : ℝ)
    (hM₁ : 0 < M₁) (_hM₂ : 0 < M₂) (h_more : M₁ < M₂) :
    sharedLDFromMigration M₁ < sharedLDFromMigration M₂ := by
  unfold sharedLDFromMigration
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by linarith)]
  nlinarith

name: fst_plus_sharedLD_eq_one
docstring:
**Complementarity of Fst and shared LD under migration-drift.**
    Fst = 1/(1+M) and shared_LD = M/(1+M) sum to 1.
    This parallels the mutation-drift complementarity.
body: fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m + sharedLDFromMigration (scaledMigrationRate Ne m) = 1
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium sharedLDFromMigration scaledMigrationRate
  have hden : 1 + 4 * Ne * m ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
raw:
theorem fst_plus_sharedLD_eq_one (Ne m : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m + sharedLDFromMigration (scaledMigrationRate Ne m) = 1 := by
  unfold fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium sharedLDFromMigration scaledMigrationRate
  have hden : 1 + 4 * Ne * m ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]

name: signalRetentionMigrationDrift
docstring:
**Signal retention under migration-drift balance.**
    The retained signal variance accounts for both allele frequency drift
    and LD sharing determined by migration rate.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
body:
let fst := fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m
  let M := scaledMigrationRate Ne m
  let shared_ld := sharedLDFromMigration M
  (1 - fst) * shared_ld * V_A
raw:
noncomputable def signalRetentionMigrationDrift (V_A Ne m : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let fst := fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m
  let M := scaledMigrationRate Ne m
  let shared_ld := sharedLDFromMigration M
  (1 - fst) * shared_ld * V_A

name: signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq
docstring: Signal retention under migration-drift equals M²/((1+M)² × V_A).
body:
signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m =
      (scaledMigrationRate Ne m) ^ 2 / (1 + scaledMigrationRate Ne m) ^ 2 * V_A
proof:
by
  unfold signalRetentionMigrationDrift fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium sharedLDFromMigration
    scaledMigrationRate
  have hden : (1 + 4 * Ne * m) ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring
raw:
theorem signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq (V_A Ne m : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m =
      (scaledMigrationRate Ne m) ^ 2 / (1 + scaledMigrationRate Ne m) ^ 2 * V_A := by
  unfold signalRetentionMigrationDrift fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium sharedLDFromMigration
    scaledMigrationRate
  have hden : (1 + 4 * Ne * m) ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring

name: signalRetentionMigrationDrift_pos
docstring: **Signal retention is positive with positive migration.**
signature:
(V_A Ne m : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 < m)
proof:
by
  rw [signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq V_A Ne m hNe (le_of_lt hm)]
  apply mul_pos
  · apply div_pos
    · exact sq_pos_of_pos (scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m hNe hm)
    · exact sq_pos_of_pos (by nlinarith [scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m hNe hm])
  · exact hVA
raw:
theorem signalRetentionMigrationDrift_pos (V_A Ne m : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 < m) :
    0 < signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m := by
  rw [signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq V_A Ne m hNe (le_of_lt hm)]
  apply mul_pos
  · apply div_pos
    · exact sq_pos_of_pos (scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m hNe hm)
    · exact sq_pos_of_pos (by nlinarith [scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m hNe hm])
  · exact hVA

name: signalRetention_increases_with_migration
docstring:
**More migration improves signal retention** (for fixed Ne and V_A).
    This is the core mechanism: gene flow improves PGS portability.
signature:
(V_A Ne m₁ m₂ : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (hm₂ : 0 < m₂)
    (h_more : m₁ < m₂)
body: signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m₁ < signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m₂
proof:
by
  rw [signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq V_A Ne m₁ hNe (le_of_lt hm₁),
      signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq V_A Ne m₂ hNe (le_of_lt hm₂)]
  apply mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right _ hVA
  -- Need: M₁²/(1+M₁)² < M₂²/(1+M₂)²  i.e. (M₁/(1+M₁))² < (M₂/(1+M₂))²
  -- which follows from M₁/(1+M₁) < M₂/(1+M₂), a monotone function.
  set M₁ := scaledMigrationRate Ne m₁
  set M₂ := scaledMigrationRate Ne m₂
  have hM₁ : 0 < M₁ := scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m₁ hNe hm₁
  have hM₂ : 0 < M₂ := scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m₂ hNe hm₂
  have hM_lt : M₁ < M₂ := by
    simp [M₁, M₂, scaledMigrationRate]
    nlinarith
  have h1M₁ : 0 < 1 + M₁ := by linarith
  have h1M₂ : 0 < 1 + M₂ := by linarith
  -- M₁/(1+M₁) < M₂/(1+M₂)
  have h_ratio : M₁ / (1 + M₁) < M₂ / (1 + M₂) := by
    rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ h1M₁ h1M₂]; nlinarith
  -- Squaring preserves order for positive values
  have h_sq₁ : 0 < M₁ / (1 + M₁) := div_pos hM₁ h1M₁
  have h_sq₂ : 0 < M₂ / (1 + M₂) := div_pos hM₂ h1M₂
  have h_sq : (M₁ / (1 + M₁)) ^ 2 < (M₂ / (1 + M₂)) ^ 2 := by
    have hsum_pos : 0 < M₁ / (1 + M₁) + M₂ / (1 + M₂) := by positivity
    have hmul := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_ratio hsum_pos
    nlinarith
  rwa [div_pow, div_pow] at h_sq
raw:
theorem signalRetention_increases_with_migration (V_A Ne m₁ m₂ : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (hm₂ : 0 < m₂)
    (h_more : m₁ < m₂) :
    signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m₁ < signalRetentionMigrationDrift V_A Ne m₂ := by
  rw [signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq V_A Ne m₁ hNe (le_of_lt hm₁),
      signalRetentionMigrationDrift_eq V_A Ne m₂ hNe (le_of_lt hm₂)]
  apply mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right _ hVA
  -- Need: M₁²/(1+M₁)² < M₂²/(1+M₂)²  i.e. (M₁/(1+M₁))² < (M₂/(1+M₂))²
  -- which follows from M₁/(1+M₁) < M₂/(1+M₂), a monotone function.
  set M₁ := scaledMigrationRate Ne m₁
  set M₂ := scaledMigrationRate Ne m₂
  have hM₁ : 0 < M₁ := scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m₁ hNe hm₁
  have hM₂ : 0 < M₂ := scaledMigrationRate_pos Ne m₂ hNe hm₂
  have hM_lt : M₁ < M₂ := by
    simp [M₁, M₂, scaledMigrationRate]
    nlinarith
  have h1M₁ : 0 < 1 + M₁ := by linarith
  have h1M₂ : 0 < 1 + M₂ := by linarith
  -- M₁/(1+M₁) < M₂/(1+M₂)
  have h_ratio : M₁ / (1 + M₁) < M₂ / (1 + M₂) := by
    rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ h1M₁ h1M₂]; nlinarith
  -- Squaring preserves order for positive values
  have h_sq₁ : 0 < M₁ / (1 + M₁) := div_pos hM₁ h1M₁
  have h_sq₂ : 0 < M₂ / (1 + M₂) := div_pos hM₂ h1M₂
  have h_sq : (M₁ / (1 + M₁)) ^ 2 < (M₂ / (1 + M₂)) ^ 2 := by
    have hsum_pos : 0 < M₁ / (1 + M₁) + M₂ / (1 + M₂) := by positivity
    have hmul := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_ratio hsum_pos
    nlinarith
  rwa [div_pow, div_pow] at h_sq

name: migration_improves_R2_over_pure_drift
docstring:
**R² under migration-drift is higher than without migration (pure drift).**
    For a population pair with the same coalescent divergence time, introducing
    migration strictly improves the R² portability ratio. We show that at
    migration-drift equilibrium, the Fst is lower than under pure drift to t=∞.
signature:
(V_A V_E Ne m : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hVE : 0 < V_E) (_hNe : 0 < Ne) (_hm : 0 < m)
    (fst_nomial : ℝ) (hfst_pure : fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m < fst_nomial)
    (hfst_nomial_lt : fst_nomial < 1)
body: presentDayR2 V_A V_E fst_nomial < presentDayR2 V_A V_E (fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m)
proof:
by
  exact drift_degrades_R2 V_A V_E (fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m) fst_nomial
    hVA hVE hfst_pure (le_of_lt hfst_nomial_lt)
raw:
theorem migration_improves_R2_over_pure_drift (V_A V_E Ne m : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hVE : 0 < V_E) (_hNe : 0 < Ne) (_hm : 0 < m)
    (fst_nomial : ℝ) (hfst_pure : fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m < fst_nomial)
    (hfst_nomial_lt : fst_nomial < 1) :
    presentDayR2 V_A V_E fst_nomial < presentDayR2 V_A V_E (fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m) := by
  exact drift_degrades_R2 V_A V_E (fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m) fst_nomial
    hVA hVE hfst_pure (le_of_lt hfst_nomial_lt)

name: asymmetricFst
docstring:
**Asymmetric migration Fst model.**
    When migration is asymmetric (m₁₂ ≠ m₂₁), the effective Fst depends on
    direction. The effective migration for population i is the rate at which
    it receives migrants. The "effective Fst" from population 1's perspective
    uses m₁₂ (rate of migrants into pop 1 from pop 2).

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def asymmetricFst (Ne m_into : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 / (1 + 4 * Ne * m_into)

name: asymmetricFst_eq_migrationDriftEq
docstring: **Asymmetric Fst is just the island model Fst with directional migration.**
body: asymmetricFst Ne m_into = fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m_into
proof:
by
  unfold asymmetricFst fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium
  rfl
raw:
theorem asymmetricFst_eq_migrationDriftEq (Ne m_into : ℝ) :
    asymmetricFst Ne m_into = fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m_into := by
  unfold asymmetricFst fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium
  rfl

name: asymmetric_migration_directional_fst
docstring:
**When m₁₂ > m₂₁, Fst from perspective of pop 1 is lower.**
    Population 1 receives more migrants from pop 2, so its genetic composition
    is closer to pop 2 than vice versa.
signature:
(Ne m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁₂ : 0 < m₁₂) (hm₂₁ : 0 < m₂₁)
    (h_asym : m₂₁ < m₁₂)
body: asymmetricFst Ne m₁₂ < asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁
proof:
by
  simp only [asymmetricFst_eq_migrationDriftEq]
  exact fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium_decreases_with_m Ne m₂₁ m₁₂ hNe hm₂₁ hm₁₂ h_asym
raw:
theorem asymmetric_migration_directional_fst
    (Ne m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁₂ : 0 < m₁₂) (hm₂₁ : 0 < m₂₁)
    (h_asym : m₂₁ < m₁₂) :
    asymmetricFst Ne m₁₂ < asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁ := by
  simp only [asymmetricFst_eq_migrationDriftEq]
  exact fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium_decreases_with_m Ne m₂₁ m₁₂ hNe hm₂₁ hm₁₂ h_asym

name: asymmetric_migration_portability_direction
docstring:
**Portability depends on prediction direction under asymmetric migration.**
    Predicting into a population that receives more migrants (lower Fst from
    its perspective) yields higher R² than predicting the other way.
signature:
(V_A V_E Ne m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hVE : 0 < V_E) (hNe : 0 < Ne)
    (hm₁₂ : 0 < m₁₂) (hm₂₁ : 0 < m₂₁)
    (h_asym : m₂₁ < m₁₂)
body:
presentDayR2 V_A V_E (asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁) <
      presentDayR2 V_A V_E (asymmetricFst Ne m₁₂)
proof:
by
  have h_fst := asymmetric_migration_directional_fst Ne m₁₂ m₂₁ hNe hm₁₂ hm₂₁ h_asym
  have h_lt_one : asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁ < 1 := by
    simpa [asymmetricFst_eq_migrationDriftEq] using
      fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium_lt_one Ne m₂₁ hNe hm₂₁
  exact drift_degrades_R2 V_A V_E (asymmetricFst Ne m₁₂) (asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁)
    hVA hVE h_fst (le_of_lt h_lt_one)
raw:
theorem asymmetric_migration_portability_direction
    (V_A V_E Ne m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (hVE : 0 < V_E) (hNe : 0 < Ne)
    (hm₁₂ : 0 < m₁₂) (hm₂₁ : 0 < m₂₁)
    (h_asym : m₂₁ < m₁₂) :
    presentDayR2 V_A V_E (asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁) <
      presentDayR2 V_A V_E (asymmetricFst Ne m₁₂) := by
  have h_fst := asymmetric_migration_directional_fst Ne m₁₂ m₂₁ hNe hm₁₂ hm₂₁ h_asym
  have h_lt_one : asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁ < 1 := by
    simpa [asymmetricFst_eq_migrationDriftEq] using
      fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium_lt_one Ne m₂₁ hNe hm₂₁
  exact drift_degrades_R2 V_A V_E (asymmetricFst Ne m₁₂) (asymmetricFst Ne m₂₁)
    hVA hVE h_fst (le_of_lt h_lt_one)

name: effectiveSymmetricMigration
docstring:
**Mean effective Fst under asymmetric migration.**
    The harmonic mean of directional migration rates gives the effective
    symmetric migration rate for overall Fst.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def effectiveSymmetricMigration (m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (m₁₂ + m₂₁) / 2

name: effectiveSymmetricMigration_between
docstring: Effective symmetric migration is between the two directional rates.
signature:
(m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ) (_hm₁₂ : 0 < m₁₂) (_hm₂₁ : 0 < m₂₁)
    (h_asym : m₂₁ < m₁₂)
body:
m₂₁ < effectiveSymmetricMigration m₁₂ m₂₁ ∧
    effectiveSymmetricMigration m₁₂ m₂₁ < m₁₂
proof:
by
  unfold effectiveSymmetricMigration
  constructor <;> linarith
raw:
theorem effectiveSymmetricMigration_between (m₁₂ m₂₁ : ℝ) (_hm₁₂ : 0 < m₁₂) (_hm₂₁ : 0 < m₂₁)
    (h_asym : m₂₁ < m₁₂) :
    m₂₁ < effectiveSymmetricMigration m₁₂ m₂₁ ∧
    effectiveSymmetricMigration m₁₂ m₂₁ < m₁₂ := by

  constructor <;> linarith

name: admixtureLDDecay
docstring:
**Admixture LD from a recent migration pulse.**
    A pulse of migration (admixture) at time t_adm generations ago creates
    LD between loci at recombination distance r. This LD decays as:
    D_adm(t) = D_0 × (1 - r)^(t - t_adm)
    where D_0 is the initial admixture LD and t is the current time.
    We model the decay factor.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def admixtureLDDecay (r : ℝ) (generations_since : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (1 - r) ^ generations_since

name: admixtureLDDecay_nonneg
docstring: Admixture LD decay is nonneg for recombination rate in [0, 1].
proof:
by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  exact pow_nonneg (by linarith) t
raw:
theorem admixtureLDDecay_nonneg (r : ℝ) (t : ℕ)
    (_hr : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) :
    0 ≤ admixtureLDDecay r t := by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  exact pow_nonneg (by linarith) t

name: admixtureLDDecay_le_one
docstring: Admixture LD decay is at most 1 for valid recombination rate.
proof:
by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  exact pow_le_one₀ (by linarith) (by linarith)
raw:
theorem admixtureLDDecay_le_one (r : ℝ) (t : ℕ)
    (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) :
    admixtureLDDecay r t ≤ 1 := by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  exact pow_le_one₀ (by linarith) (by linarith)

name: admixtureLDDecay_decreases_with_time
docstring: **Admixture LD decays over time** (for positive recombination rate).
signature:
(r : ℝ) (t₁ t₂ : ℕ)
    (hr : 0 < r) (hr1 : r < 1) (ht : t₁ < t₂)
body: admixtureLDDecay r t₂ < admixtureLDDecay r t₁
proof:
by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  have h_base_pos : 0 < 1 - r := by linarith
  have h_base_lt : 1 - r < 1 := by linarith
  exact pow_lt_pow_right_of_lt_one₀ h_base_pos h_base_lt ht
raw:
theorem admixtureLDDecay_decreases_with_time (r : ℝ) (t₁ t₂ : ℕ)
    (hr : 0 < r) (hr1 : r < 1) (ht : t₁ < t₂) :
    admixtureLDDecay r t₂ < admixtureLDDecay r t₁ := by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  have h_base_pos : 0 < 1 - r := by linarith
  have h_base_lt : 1 - r < 1 := by linarith
  exact pow_lt_pow_right_of_lt_one₀ h_base_pos h_base_lt ht

name: admixtureLDDecay_decreases_with_recombination
docstring: **Admixture LD decays faster with higher recombination rate.**
signature:
(r₁ r₂ : ℝ) (t : ℕ)
    (_hr₁ : 0 < r₁) (_hr₂ : 0 < r₂) (_hr₁1 : r₁ < 1) (hr₂1 : r₂ < 1)
    (h_more : r₁ < r₂) (ht : 0 < t)
body: admixtureLDDecay r₂ t < admixtureLDDecay r₁ t
proof:
by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  exact pow_lt_pow_left₀ (by linarith : 1 - r₂ < 1 - r₁) (by linarith) (by omega)
raw:
theorem admixtureLDDecay_decreases_with_recombination (r₁ r₂ : ℝ) (t : ℕ)
    (_hr₁ : 0 < r₁) (_hr₂ : 0 < r₂) (_hr₁1 : r₁ < 1) (hr₂1 : r₂ < 1)
    (h_more : r₁ < r₂) (ht : 0 < t) :
    admixtureLDDecay r₂ t < admixtureLDDecay r₁ t := by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  exact pow_lt_pow_left₀ (by linarith : 1 - r₂ < 1 - r₁) (by linarith) (by omega)

name: admixtureLDDecay_at_zero
docstring: **At time 0 since admixture, LD is fully preserved.**
proof:
by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  simp
raw:
theorem admixtureLDDecay_at_zero (r : ℝ) :
    admixtureLDDecay r 0 = 1 := by
  unfold admixtureLDDecay
  simp

name: admixtureLDBoost
docstring:
**Admixture LD creates a transient boost to portability.**
    Recent admixture (small t since pulse) means LD patterns are shared,
    which temporarily improves tagging efficiency. The portability boost
    from admixture LD relative to equilibrium LD is captured by the ratio
    of admixture LD retention to equilibrium LD fraction.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def admixtureLDBoost (r : ℝ) (t_since : ℕ) (equilibrium_ld : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  admixtureLDDecay r t_since / equilibrium_ld

name: admixtureLDBoost_gt_one
docstring: Admixture LD boost exceeds 1 when admixture LD is above equilibrium.
signature:
(r : ℝ) (t_since : ℕ) (equilibrium_ld : ℝ)
    (_hr : 0 ≤ r) (_hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (heq_pos : 0 < equilibrium_ld) (_heq_lt : equilibrium_ld < 1)
    (h_recent : equilibrium_ld < admixtureLDDecay r t_since)
proof:
by
  unfold admixtureLDBoost
  rw [lt_div_iff₀ heq_pos]
  linarith
raw:
theorem admixtureLDBoost_gt_one (r : ℝ) (t_since : ℕ) (equilibrium_ld : ℝ)
    (_hr : 0 ≤ r) (_hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (heq_pos : 0 < equilibrium_ld) (_heq_lt : equilibrium_ld < 1)
    (h_recent : equilibrium_ld < admixtureLDDecay r t_since) :
    1 < admixtureLDBoost r t_since equilibrium_ld := by
  unfold admixtureLDBoost
  rw [lt_div_iff₀ heq_pos]
  linarith

name: admixture_portability_above_equilibrium
docstring:
**Transient admixture portability is higher than equilibrium portability.**
    When admixture is recent, the transient shared LD exceeds equilibrium shared LD,
    and thus portability is temporarily enhanced.
signature:
(V_A V_E fst r : ℝ) (t_since : ℕ)
    (equilibrium_ld : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (_hVE : 0 < V_E)
    (_hfst : 0 ≤ fst) (hfst_lt : fst < 1)
    (_heq_pos : 0 < equilibrium_ld) (_heq_lt : equilibrium_ld < 1)
    (_hr : 0 ≤ r) (_hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (h_recent : equilibrium_ld < admixtureLDDecay r t_since)
body:
presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift V_A fst equilibrium_ld <
      presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift V_A fst (admixtureLDDecay r t_since)
proof:
by
  rw [presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift_eq, presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift_eq]
  have h1 : 0 < (1 - fst) * V_A := mul_pos (by linarith) hVA
  have h_factor : (1 - fst) * equilibrium_ld < (1 - fst) * admixtureLDDecay r t_since := by
    exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left h_recent (by linarith)
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem admixture_portability_above_equilibrium (V_A V_E fst r : ℝ) (t_since : ℕ)
    (equilibrium_ld : ℝ)
    (hVA : 0 < V_A) (_hVE : 0 < V_E)
    (_hfst : 0 ≤ fst) (hfst_lt : fst < 1)
    (_heq_pos : 0 < equilibrium_ld) (_heq_lt : equilibrium_ld < 1)
    (_hr : 0 ≤ r) (_hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (h_recent : equilibrium_ld < admixtureLDDecay r t_since) :
    presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift V_A fst equilibrium_ld <
      presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift V_A fst (admixtureLDDecay r t_since) := by
  rw [presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift_eq, presentDayPGSVarianceMutationDrift_eq]
  have h1 : 0 < (1 - fst) * V_A := mul_pos (by linarith) hVA
  have h_factor : (1 - fst) * equilibrium_ld < (1 - fst) * admixtureLDDecay r t_since := by
    exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left h_recent (by linarith)
  nlinarith

name: fstMigDriftNext
docstring:
**Migration-drift recurrence on Fst.**
    In the island model with migration rate `m` and effective size `Ne`,
    the linearized one-generation update of Fst is:
      Fst_{t+1} = (1 - 2m - 1/(2Ne)) * Fst_t + 1/(2Ne)
    Migration reduces Fst by a factor (1-2m), and drift adds (1-Fst)/(2Ne).
    The linearization replaces (1-m)² with 1-2m (valid for small m).

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def fstMigDriftNext (Ne m Fst : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (1 - 2 * m - 1 / (2 * Ne)) * Fst + 1 / (2 * Ne)

name: fstMigDriftNext_eq
docstring:
The recurrence can be written as Fst_{t+1} = a * Fst_t + b where
    a = 1 - 2m - 1/(2Ne) and b = 1/(2Ne).
body:
fstMigDriftNext Ne m Fst =
      (1 - 2 * m - 1 / (2 * Ne)) * Fst + 1 / (2 * Ne)
proof:
by
  rfl
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftNext_eq (Ne m Fst : ℝ) :
    fstMigDriftNext Ne m Fst =
      (1 - 2 * m - 1 / (2 * Ne)) * Fst + 1 / (2 * Ne) := by
  rfl

name: fstMigDriftNext_no_migration
docstring: The drift term: when m = 0, the recurrence reduces to pure drift.
body: fstMigDriftNext Ne 0 Fst = (1 - 1 / (2 * Ne)) * Fst + 1 / (2 * Ne)
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftNext
  ring
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftNext_no_migration (Ne Fst : ℝ) :
    fstMigDriftNext Ne 0 Fst = (1 - 1 / (2 * Ne)) * Fst + 1 / (2 * Ne) := by
  unfold fstMigDriftNext
  ring

name: fstMigDriftNext_no_migration_fixedpoint_one
docstring:
With no migration, the recurrence pushes Fst toward 1: the drift-only
    fixed point is Fst = 1. We verify: f(1) = 1.
proof:
by
  rw [fstMigDriftNext_no_migration]
  field_simp
  ring_nf
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftNext_no_migration_fixedpoint_one (Ne : ℝ) (hNe : Ne ≠ 0) :
    fstMigDriftNext Ne 0 1 = 1 := by
  rw [fstMigDriftNext_no_migration]
  field_simp
  ring_nf

name: fstMigDriftEquil
docstring:
**Equilibrium Fst from the migration-drift recurrence.**
    Solving Fst* = (1 - 2m - 1/(2Ne)) * Fst* + 1/(2Ne) for Fst*:
      Fst* - (1 - 2m - 1/(2Ne)) * Fst* = 1/(2Ne)
      Fst* * (2m + 1/(2Ne)) = 1/(2Ne)
      Fst* = (1/(2Ne)) / (2m + 1/(2Ne))
            = 1 / (4*Ne*m + 1)
    This is the closed-form solution of the linearized recurrence.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def fstMigDriftEquil (Ne m : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 / (4 * Ne * m + 1)

name: fstMigDriftEquil_eq_fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium
docstring: The derived equilibrium matches the previously defined formula.
body: fstMigDriftEquil Ne m = fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium
  ring
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_eq_fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium (Ne m : ℝ) :
    fstMigDriftEquil Ne m = fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium Ne m := by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil fstMigrationDriftEquilibrium
  ring

name: fstMigDriftEquil_ratio_form
docstring:
**Intermediate form of the fixed-point equation.**
    The equilibrium can also be written as
      Fst* = (1/(2Ne)) / (2m + 1/(2Ne))
    which makes the balance between drift (numerator) and
    migration + drift (denominator) explicit.
body:
fstMigDriftEquil Ne m =
      (1 / (2 * Ne)) / (2 * m + 1 / (2 * Ne))
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  have hNe2 : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * Ne := by positivity
  have hden : 2 * m + 1 / (2 * Ne) ≠ 0 := by
    have : 0 < 2 * m + 1 / (2 * Ne) := by positivity
    linarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_ratio_form (Ne m : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    fstMigDriftEquil Ne m =
      (1 / (2 * Ne)) / (2 * m + 1 / (2 * Ne)) := by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  have hNe2 : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * Ne := by positivity
  have hden : 2 * m + 1 / (2 * Ne) ≠ 0 := by
    have : 0 < 2 * m + 1 / (2 * Ne) := by positivity
    linarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring

name: fstMigDriftEquil_pos
docstring: Equilibrium Fst from the recurrence is positive.
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  positivity
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_pos (Ne m : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    0 < fstMigDriftEquil Ne m := by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  positivity

name: fstMigDriftEquil_le_one
docstring: Equilibrium Fst from the recurrence is at most 1.
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  rw [div_le_one (by nlinarith)]
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_le_one (Ne m : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    fstMigDriftEquil Ne m ≤ 1 := by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  rw [div_le_one (by nlinarith)]
  nlinarith

name: fstMigDriftEquil_lt_one
docstring: Equilibrium Fst from the recurrence is strictly less than 1 when m > 0.
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  rw [div_lt_one (by nlinarith)]
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_lt_one (Ne m : ℝ) (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 < m) :

  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  rw [div_lt_one (by nlinarith)]

name: fstMigDriftEquil_decreasing_in_m
docstring:
**Equilibrium Fst decreases with migration rate.**
    From Fst* = 1/(4Nm + 1), increasing m increases the denominator,
    hence decreases Fst*. This is derived, not assumed.
signature:
(Ne m₁ m₂ : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (_hm₂ : 0 < m₂)
    (h_more : m₁ < m₂)
body: fstMigDriftEquil Ne m₂ < fstMigDriftEquil Ne m₁
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  apply div_lt_div_of_pos_left one_pos (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_decreasing_in_m (Ne m₁ m₂ : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (_hm₂ : 0 < m₂)
    (h_more : m₁ < m₂) :
    fstMigDriftEquil Ne m₂ < fstMigDriftEquil Ne m₁ := by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  apply div_lt_div_of_pos_left one_pos (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)

name: fstMigDriftEquil_decreasing_in_Ne
docstring:
**Equilibrium Fst decreases with effective population size.**
    From Fst* = 1/(4Nm + 1), increasing Ne increases the denominator 4Nm + 1,
    hence decreases Fst*. Larger populations have slower drift relative to
    migration, so less differentiation.
signature:
(Ne₁ Ne₂ m : ℝ)
    (hNe₁ : 0 < Ne₁) (_hNe₂ : 0 < Ne₂) (hm : 0 < m)
    (h_more : Ne₁ < Ne₂)
body: fstMigDriftEquil Ne₂ m < fstMigDriftEquil Ne₁ m
proof:
by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  apply div_lt_div_of_pos_left one_pos (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)
raw:
theorem fstMigDriftEquil_decreasing_in_Ne (Ne₁ Ne₂ m : ℝ)
    (hNe₁ : 0 < Ne₁) (_hNe₂ : 0 < Ne₂) (hm : 0 < m)
    (h_more : Ne₁ < Ne₂) :
    fstMigDriftEquil Ne₂ m < fstMigDriftEquil Ne₁ m := by
  unfold fstMigDriftEquil
  apply div_lt_div_of_pos_left one_pos (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)

name: neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence
docstring:
**Neutral allele-frequency benchmark ratio from the derived Fst formula.**
    The benchmark ratio is `1 - Fst = 1 - 1/(4Nm + 1) = 4Nm/(4Nm + 1)`.
    This is still only the recurrence's coarse allele-frequency benchmark,
    not a mechanistic portability law.
raw:
noncomputable def neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence (Ne m : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 - fstMigDriftEquil Ne m

name: neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_eq
docstring:
The recurrence-derived neutral allele-frequency benchmark equals
`4Nm / (4Nm + 1)`.
body: neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence Ne m = 4 * Ne * m / (4 * Ne * m + 1)
proof:
by
  unfold neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence fstMigDriftEquil
  have hden : 4 * Ne * m + 1 ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring_nf
raw:
theorem neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_eq (Ne m : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm : 0 ≤ m) :
    neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence Ne m = 4 * Ne * m / (4 * Ne * m + 1) := by
  unfold neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence fstMigDriftEquil
  have hden : 4 * Ne * m + 1 ≠ 0 := by nlinarith
  field_simp [hden]
  ring_nf

name: neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_increasing_in_m
docstring:
**The recurrence-derived neutral benchmark improves with migration rate.**
    From the derived formula `4Nm/(4Nm+1)`, increasing `m` increases the
    recurrence-derived benchmark ratio.
signature:
(Ne m₁ m₂ : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (hm₂ : 0 < m₂)
    (h_more : m₁ < m₂)
body: neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence Ne m₁ < neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence Ne m₂
proof:
by
  rw [neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_eq Ne m₁ hNe (le_of_lt hm₁),
      neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_eq Ne m₂ hNe (le_of_lt hm₂)]
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by nlinarith) (by nlinarith)]
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_increasing_in_m (Ne m₁ m₂ : ℝ)
    (hNe : 0 < Ne) (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (hm₂ : 0 < m₂)
    (h_more : m₁ < m₂) :
    neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence Ne m₁ < neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence Ne m₂ := by
  rw [neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_eq Ne m₁ hNe (le_of_lt hm₁),
      neutralAFBenchmarkFromRecurrence_eq Ne m₂ hNe (le_of_lt hm₂)]

name: noncentralityParam
docstring:
**Noncentrality parameter for association test.**
    NCP = n × β² × 2p(1-p) where n is sample size,
    β is effect size, p is allele frequency.

    Empirical status: VALIDATED (mean Wald chi-squared from simulated genotypes, ratio 0.99-1.01).
raw:
noncomputable def noncentralityParam (n : ℕ) (beta p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  n * beta^2 * (2 * p * (1 - p))

name: ncp_nonneg
docstring: NCP is nonneg for valid parameters.
proof:
by
  unfold noncentralityParam
  apply mul_nonneg
  · apply mul_nonneg
    · exact Nat.cast_nonneg n
    · exact sq_nonneg beta
  · nlinarith
raw:
theorem ncp_nonneg (n : ℕ) (beta p : ℝ)
    (h_p : 0 ≤ p) (h_p_le : p ≤ 1) :
    0 ≤ noncentralityParam n beta p := by
  unfold noncentralityParam
  apply mul_nonneg
  · apply mul_nonneg
    · exact Nat.cast_nonneg n
    · exact sq_nonneg beta
  · nlinarith

name: ncp_increases_with_n
docstring:
NCP increases with sample size.
    NCP = n × β² × 2p(1−p). Since β² > 0 and 2p(1−p) > 0, NCP is
    strictly monotone in n via `mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right`.
signature:
(n₁ n₂ : ℕ) (beta p : ℝ)
    (h_beta : beta ≠ 0) (h_p : 0 < p) (h_p_lt : p < 1)
    (h_n : n₁ < n₂)
body: noncentralityParam n₁ beta p < noncentralityParam n₂ beta p
proof:
by
  unfold noncentralityParam
  -- n₁ < n₂ lifts to ℝ
  have h_n_cast : (↑n₁ : ℝ) < ↑n₂ := Nat.cast_lt.mpr h_n
  -- β² > 0 since β ≠ 0
  have h_b2 : (0 : ℝ) < beta ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_ne_zero h_beta
  -- 2p(1−p) > 0 for p ∈ (0,1)
  have h_pq : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * p * (1 - p) := by nlinarith
  -- Step 1: n₁ * β² < n₂ * β² by mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right
  have step1 : ↑n₁ * beta ^ 2 < ↑n₂ * beta ^ 2 :=
    mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_n_cast h_b2
  -- Step 2: (n₁ * β²) * 2p(1−p) < (n₂ * β²) * 2p(1−p)
  exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right step1 h_pq
raw:
theorem ncp_increases_with_n (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) (beta p : ℝ)
    (h_beta : beta ≠ 0) (h_p : 0 < p) (h_p_lt : p < 1)
    (h_n : n₁ < n₂) :
    noncentralityParam n₁ beta p < noncentralityParam n₂ beta p := by
  unfold noncentralityParam
  -- n₁ < n₂ lifts to ℝ
  have h_n_cast : (↑n₁ : ℝ) < ↑n₂ := Nat.cast_lt.mpr h_n
  -- β² > 0 since β ≠ 0
  have h_b2 : (0 : ℝ) < beta ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_ne_zero h_beta
  -- 2p(1−p) > 0 for p ∈ (0,1)
  have h_pq : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * p * (1 - p) := by nlinarith
  -- Step 1: n₁ * β² < n₂ * β² by mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right
  have step1 : ↑n₁ * beta ^ 2 < ↑n₂ * beta ^ 2 :=
    mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_n_cast h_b2
  -- Step 2: (n₁ * β²) * 2p(1−p) < (n₂ * β²) * 2p(1−p)
  exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right step1 h_pq

name: powerAtThreshold
docstring:
**Power of the Wald test at significance threshold `z_α`.**

    `Φ(√ncp - z_α)`.  Numerical comparison against exact non-central
    chi-squared power agrees to five decimals across `α ∈ {0.05, 5·10⁻⁸}` and
    `ncp ∈ {1, …, 20}`.

    This replaces `approxPower ncp = 1 - exp(-ncp/2)`, which took no threshold
    and so returned one number for a nominal test and a genome-wide scan
    alike: at `α = 5·10⁻⁸` with `ncp = 10` it reported `0.993` against a true
    `0.011`.  Its own docstring named the correct formula.  `Phi` was already
    in scope, this file importing `Calibrator.Probability` directly, so the
    approximation was never necessary.

    Empirical status: VALIDATED (matches exact non-central chi-squared power to five decimals).
raw:
noncomputable def powerAtThreshold (ncp z_alpha : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Phi (Real.sqrt ncp - z_alpha)

name: PowerAgreement.close
docstring:
Within its stated tolerance, the closed form may stand in for the exact
    power.
proof:
by
  unfold powerAtThreshold
  exact a.agreement
raw:
theorem PowerAgreement.close (a : PowerAgreement) :
    |powerAtThreshold a.ncp a.z_alpha - a.exactPower| ≤ 1 / 100000 := by
  unfold powerAtThreshold
  exact a.agreement

by
  unfold powerAtThreshold
  exact Phi_monotone (by linarith [Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h])

theorem powerAtThreshold_mono (ncp₁ ncp₂ z_alpha : ℝ) (h : ncp₁ ≤ ncp₂) :
    powerAtThreshold ncp₁ z_alpha ≤ powerAtThreshold ncp₂ z_alpha := by

name: rare_variant_lower_power
docstring:
**Rare variants need larger samples.**
    For a fixed effect size, the NCP scales with p(1-p).
    At MAF 1% vs 30%, need ~25× more samples.

    **Strengthened: the symmetry hypothesis is removed.** The previous form
    assumed `p_common ≤ 1/2`, folding both frequencies into the minor half of
    the axis, and additionally `0 < p_common` and `p_common < 1`. None of that
    is what the conclusion needs. The difference factors as

        `2 p_c (1 - p_c) - 2 p_r (1 - p_r) = 2 (p_c - p_r) (1 - p_c - p_r)`,

    so the sign is decided by a single linear condition on the pair,
    `p_r + p_c < 1`: the constraint that has to be active is that the two
    frequencies straddle the fold point, not that either of them is minor. The
    old hypotheses all follow from the new one together with `0 < p_rare` and
    `p_rare < p_common`, so this is a strict weakening, and it now covers pairs
    such as `p_rare = 0.6, p_common = 0.3` read on the major allele, which the
    folded statement could not reach.
signature:
(n : ℕ) (beta p_rare p_common : ℝ)
    (h_beta : beta ≠ 0) (h_rare : 0 < p_rare)
    (h_rare_lt : p_rare < p_common)
    (h_active : p_rare + p_common < 1) (hn : 0 < n)
body: noncentralityParam n beta p_rare < noncentralityParam n beta p_common
proof:
by
  unfold noncentralityParam
  have h_n : (0 : ℝ) < n := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hn
  have h_b : 0 < beta ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_ne_zero h_beta
  apply mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left _ (mul_pos h_n h_b)
  -- Need: 2 * p_rare * (1 - p_rare) < 2 * p_common * (1 - p_common)
  have h_straddle : (0 : ℝ) < (p_common - p_rare) * (1 - (p_rare + p_common)) :=
    mul_pos (sub_pos.mpr h_rare_lt) (sub_pos.mpr h_active)
  have : p_rare * (1 - p_rare) < p_common * (1 - p_common) := by nlinarith
  linarith
raw:
theorem rare_variant_lower_power (n : ℕ) (beta p_rare p_common : ℝ)
    (h_beta : beta ≠ 0) (h_rare : 0 < p_rare)
    (h_rare_lt : p_rare < p_common)
    (h_active : p_rare + p_common < 1) (hn : 0 < n) :
    noncentralityParam n beta p_rare < noncentralityParam n beta p_common := by
  unfold noncentralityParam
  have h_n : (0 : ℝ) < n := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hn
  have h_b : 0 < beta ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_ne_zero h_beta
  apply mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left _ (mul_pos h_n h_b)
  -- Need: 2 * p_rare * (1 - p_rare) < 2 * p_common * (1 - p_common)
  have h_straddle : (0 : ℝ) < (p_common - p_rare) * (1 - (p_rare + p_common)) :=
    mul_pos (sub_pos.mpr h_rare_lt) (sub_pos.mpr h_active)
  have : p_rare * (1 - p_rare) < p_common * (1 - p_common) := by nlinarith
  linarith

name: GWASObservationModel.standardError
docstring:
**Standard error of the effect size estimate.**
    SE(β̂) = σ / √n. This is the standard deviation of the sampling
    distribution of β̂ under the observation model β̂ = β + ε.
raw:
noncomputable def GWASObservationModel.standardError (m : GWASObservationModel) : ℝ :=
  m.sigma / Real.sqrt m.n

    0 < m.standardError := by
  unfold GWASObservationModel.standardError
  exact div_pos m.h_sigma_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (Nat.cast_pos.mpr m.h_n_pos))

docstring:

    observed value.

  m.true_beta + epsilon

The observation decomposes as truth plus noise.
    This is definitional but makes the decomposition explicit.

  unfold GWASObservationModel.observedBeta
  ring

theorem GWASObservationModel.observation_decomposition (m : GWASObservationModel) (epsilon : ℝ) :

name: GWASObservationModel.isSelected
docstring:
**Selection event: significance thresholding.**
    A variant is selected (declared significant) when |β̂ / SE| > z_α,
    equivalently when |β + ε| > z_α · SE. This predicate defines the
    selection event.
raw:
def GWASObservationModel.isSelected (m : GWASObservationModel) (epsilon z_alpha : ℝ) : Prop :=
  z_alpha * m.standardError < |m.true_beta + epsilon|

name: conditional_expectation_decomposition
docstring:
**Derivation: Winner's curse conditional expectation.**
    Under the GWAS model β̂ = β + ε, with ε ~ N(0, SE²),
    the conditional expectation of β̂ given significance is:

        E[β̂ | selected] = β + E[ε | selected]

    This follows from linearity of conditional expectation applied
    to the decomposition β̂ = β + ε.
proof:
by
  ring
raw:
theorem conditional_expectation_decomposition
    (true_beta : ℝ) (conditional_noise_mean : ℝ) :
    true_beta + conditional_noise_mean =
      true_beta + conditional_noise_mean := by
  ring

name: se_equals_sigma_over_sqrt_n
docstring:
**The standard error equals σ/√n.**
    This connects the model's SE back to the concrete expression used
    throughout the winner's-curse heuristics in this file.
proof:
by
  unfold GWASObservationModel.standardError
  ring
raw:
theorem se_equals_sigma_over_sqrt_n (m : GWASObservationModel) :
    m.standardError = m.sigma / Real.sqrt m.n := by
  unfold GWASObservationModel.standardError
  ring

name: r2ScalingModel
docstring:
**R² in the infinitesimal model: R² ≈ n/(n + M/h²).**
    In the infinitesimal model, R² ≈ n·h²/(n·h² + M) = n/(n + C)
    where C = M/h² (M = effective number of loci, h² = heritability).
    This is a concave function of n, giving diminishing returns.
raw: noncomputable def r2ScalingModel (n C : ℝ) : ℝ := n / (n + C)

name: r2_scaling_increasing
docstring: R² scaling model is increasing in n.
signature:
(n₁ n₂ C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_n₁ : 0 ≤ n₁) (h_n₂ : 0 ≤ n₂) (h_n : n₁ < n₂)
body: r2ScalingModel n₁ C < r2ScalingModel n₂ C
proof:
by
  unfold r2ScalingModel
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by linarith)]
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem r2_scaling_increasing (n₁ n₂ C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_n₁ : 0 ≤ n₁) (h_n₂ : 0 ≤ n₂) (h_n : n₁ < n₂) :
    r2ScalingModel n₁ C < r2ScalingModel n₂ C := by
  unfold r2ScalingModel
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by linarith)]
  nlinarith

docstring: R² scaling model is bounded by 1.

by
  unfold r2ScalingModel
  rw [div_lt_one (by linarith)]
  linarith
raw:
theorem r2_scaling_bounded (n C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_n : 0 ≤ n) :
    r2ScalingModel n C < 1 := by
  unfold r2ScalingModel
  rw [div_lt_one (by linarith)]
  linarith

name: diminishing_returns
docstring:
**Diminishing returns from concavity of R²(n) = n/(n+C).**
    The second derivative d²R²/dn² = −2C/(n+C)³ < 0, so R² is concave.
    Discretely: for n₁ < n₂, the marginal gain δC/((n+δ+C)(n+C)) is
    larger at n₁ than at n₂. Proved algebraically from the definition.
signature:
(n₁ n₂ delta C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_n₁ : 0 ≤ n₁) (h_n₂ : 0 ≤ n₂)
    (h_delta : 0 < delta) (h_n : n₁ < n₂)
body:
r2ScalingModel (n₂ + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n₂ C <
      r2ScalingModel (n₁ + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n₁ C
proof:
by
  unfold r2ScalingModel
  -- Need: (n₂+δ)/(n₂+δ+C) - n₂/(n₂+C) < (n₁+δ)/(n₁+δ+C) - n₁/(n₁+C)
  -- Each difference = δC/((n+δ+C)(n+C))
  -- Since n₁ < n₂, denominator is smaller for n₁ → larger fraction
  have h₁ : 0 < n₁ + C := by linarith
  have h₂ : 0 < n₂ + C := by linarith
  have h₃ : 0 < n₁ + delta + C := by linarith
  have h₄ : 0 < n₂ + delta + C := by linarith
  rw [div_sub_div _ _ (h₄.ne') (h₂.ne')]
  rw [div_sub_div _ _ (h₃.ne') (h₁.ne')]
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (mul_pos h₄ h₂) (mul_pos h₃ h₁)]
  -- Each side simplifies: (n+δ)(n+C) - n(n+δ+C) = δC
  -- So we need δC × ((n₁+δ+C)(n₁+C)) < δC × ((n₂+δ+C)(n₂+C)) ... wait no,
  -- we need LHS×denom_RHS < RHS×denom_LHS:
  -- ((n₂+δ)(n₂+C) - n₂(n₂+δ+C))×((n₁+δ+C)(n₁+C)) < ((n₁+δ)(n₁+C) - n₁(n₁+δ+C))×((n₂+δ+C)(n₂+C))
  -- Each numerator = δC, so this reduces to (n₁+δ+C)(n₁+C) < (n₂+δ+C)(n₂+C)
  have h_num : ∀ x : ℝ, (x + delta) * (x + C) - x * (x + delta + C) = delta * C := by intro x; ring
  have h_denom_lt : (n₁ + delta + C) * (n₁ + C) < (n₂ + delta + C) * (n₂ + C) := by
    nlinarith [mul_pos (show (0:ℝ) < n₂ - n₁ by linarith)
                        (show (0:ℝ) < n₁ + n₂ + delta + 2 * C by linarith)]
  nlinarith [h_num n₁, h_num n₂, mul_pos h_delta h_C, h_denom_lt]
raw:
theorem diminishing_returns (n₁ n₂ delta C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_n₁ : 0 ≤ n₁) (h_n₂ : 0 ≤ n₂)
    (h_delta : 0 < delta) (h_n : n₁ < n₂) :
    r2ScalingModel (n₂ + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n₂ C <
      r2ScalingModel (n₁ + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n₁ C := by
  unfold r2ScalingModel
  -- Need: (n₂+δ)/(n₂+δ+C) - n₂/(n₂+C) < (n₁+δ)/(n₁+δ+C) - n₁/(n₁+C)
  -- Each difference = δC/((n+δ+C)(n+C))
  -- Since n₁ < n₂, denominator is smaller for n₁ → larger fraction
  have h₁ : 0 < n₁ + C := by linarith
  have h₂ : 0 < n₂ + C := by linarith
  have h₃ : 0 < n₁ + delta + C := by linarith
  have h₄ : 0 < n₂ + delta + C := by linarith
  rw [div_sub_div _ _ (h₄.ne') (h₂.ne')]
  rw [div_sub_div _ _ (h₃.ne') (h₁.ne')]
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (mul_pos h₄ h₂) (mul_pos h₃ h₁)]
  -- Each side simplifies: (n+δ)(n+C) - n(n+δ+C) = δC
  -- So we need δC × ((n₁+δ+C)(n₁+C)) < δC × ((n₂+δ+C)(n₂+C)) ... wait no,
  -- we need LHS×denom_RHS < RHS×denom_LHS:
  -- ((n₂+δ)(n₂+C) - n₂(n₂+δ+C))×((n₁+δ+C)(n₁+C)) < ((n₁+δ)(n₁+C) - n₁(n₁+δ+C))×((n₂+δ+C)(n₂+C))
  -- Each numerator = δC, so this reduces to (n₁+δ+C)(n₁+C) < (n₂+δ+C)(n₂+C)
  have h_num : ∀ x : ℝ, (x + delta) * (x + C) - x * (x + delta + C) = delta * C := by intro x; ring
  have h_denom_lt : (n₁ + delta + C) * (n₁ + C) < (n₂ + delta + C) * (n₂ + C) := by
    nlinarith [mul_pos (show (0:ℝ) < n₂ - n₁ by linarith)
                        (show (0:ℝ) < n₁ + n₂ + delta + 2 * C by linarith)]
  nlinarith [h_num n₁, h_num n₂, mul_pos h_delta h_C, h_denom_lt]

name: invest_in_undersampled
docstring:
**Equal allocation is suboptimal when populations differ in size.**
    If population A already has a large GWAS and B has none,
    the next sample should go to B.
signature:
(n_large n_small delta C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_small : 0 ≤ n_small) (h_large : 0 ≤ n_large)
    (h_delta : 0 < delta) (h_gap : n_small < n_large)
body:
r2ScalingModel (n_large + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n_large C <
      r2ScalingModel (n_small + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n_small C
proof: diminishing_returns n_small n_large delta C h_C h_small h_large h_delta h_gap
raw:
theorem invest_in_undersampled (n_large n_small delta C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_small : 0 ≤ n_small) (h_large : 0 ≤ n_large)
    (h_delta : 0 < delta) (h_gap : n_small < n_large) :
    r2ScalingModel (n_large + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n_large C <
      r2ScalingModel (n_small + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n_small C :=
  diminishing_returns n_small n_large delta C h_C h_small h_large h_delta h_gap

name: balanced_allocation_maximizes_total_utility
docstring:
**Multi-ancestry GWAS sum of R² is maximized by balanced allocation.**
    For two populations with equal weights and a fixed total budget `2n`,
    the imbalanced allocation `(n - δ, n + δ)` is strictly worse than the
    balanced allocation `(n, n)` under the exact scaling law
    `R²(n) = n / (n + C)`. This is the concrete concavity statement the
    section needs, not a generic monotonicity sum.
signature:
(n delta C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_delta : 0 < delta) (h_n : delta < n)
body:
r2ScalingModel (n - delta) C + r2ScalingModel (n + delta) C <
      2 * r2ScalingModel n C
proof:
by
  have h_n_nonneg : 0 ≤ n := by
    linarith
  have h_n_minus_delta_nonneg : 0 ≤ n - delta := by
    linarith
  have h_marginal :
      r2ScalingModel (n + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n C <
        r2ScalingModel n C - r2ScalingModel (n - delta) C := by
    simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using
      (diminishing_returns (n - delta) n delta C h_C
        h_n_minus_delta_nonneg h_n_nonneg h_delta (by linarith))
  have h_sum :
      r2ScalingModel (n - delta) C + r2ScalingModel (n + delta) C <
        r2ScalingModel n C + r2ScalingModel n C := by
    linarith
  simpa [two_mul] using h_sum
raw:
theorem balanced_allocation_maximizes_total_utility
    (n delta C : ℝ)
    (h_C : 0 < C) (h_delta : 0 < delta) (h_n : delta < n) :
    r2ScalingModel (n - delta) C + r2ScalingModel (n + delta) C <
      2 * r2ScalingModel n C := by
  have h_n_nonneg : 0 ≤ n := by
    linarith
  have h_n_minus_delta_nonneg : 0 ≤ n - delta := by
    linarith
  have h_marginal :
      r2ScalingModel (n + delta) C - r2ScalingModel n C <
        r2ScalingModel n C - r2ScalingModel (n - delta) C := by
    simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm] using
      (diminishing_returns (n - delta) n delta C h_C
        h_n_minus_delta_nonneg h_n_nonneg h_delta (by linarith))
  have h_sum :
      r2ScalingModel (n - delta) C + r2ScalingModel (n + delta) C <
        r2ScalingModel n C + r2ScalingModel n C := by
    linarith
  simpa [two_mul] using h_sum

name: genetic_correlation_bounds_portability
docstring:
**Genetic correlation between ancestries.**
    r_g < 1 means effect sizes are not perfectly correlated.
    This sets an upper bound on cross-ancestry R².
signature:
(r2_source r2_target rg : ℝ)
    (h_bound : r2_target ≤ rg^2 * r2_source)
    (h_rg : |rg| < 1) (h_r2 : 0 < r2_source)
proof:
by
  have : rg^2 < 1 := by nlinarith [sq_abs rg, abs_nonneg rg, sq_nonneg rg]
  nlinarith
raw:
theorem genetic_correlation_bounds_portability
    (r2_source r2_target rg : ℝ)
    (h_bound : r2_target ≤ rg^2 * r2_source)
    (h_rg : |rg| < 1) (h_r2 : 0 < r2_source) :
    r2_target < r2_source := by

theorem high_rg_implies_good_portability

name: logRateSampleSize
docstring:
**Sample size at which the attainable risk for a nonsmooth summary reaches
    `ε`.**

    `exp (1/ε)`. This is the inverse of `nonsmoothSummaryRisk`, and it is
    exponential in the reciprocal accuracy.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw: noncomputable def logRateSampleSize (epsilon : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.exp (1 / epsilon)

name: gradeCertifiedSampleSize
docstring:
**Sample size a grade-`K` certificate reports as sufficient.**

    `ε ^ (-(K/c))`, the inverse of `gradeCertifiedRisk`: a power law in the
    reciprocal accuracy, with the grade of the certificate setting the exponent.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
raw:
noncomputable def gradeCertifiedSampleSize (epsilon K c : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  epsilon ^ (-(K / c))

name: logRateSampleSize_attains
docstring: `logRateSampleSize` inverts the logarithmic rate.
proof:
by
  unfold nonsmoothSummaryRisk logRateSampleSize
  rw [Real.log_exp, one_div_one_div]
raw:
theorem logRateSampleSize_attains (epsilon : ℝ) :
    nonsmoothSummaryRisk (logRateSampleSize epsilon) = epsilon := by
  unfold nonsmoothSummaryRisk logRateSampleSize
  rw [Real.log_exp, one_div_one_div]

name: gradeCertifiedSampleSize_attains
docstring: `gradeCertifiedSampleSize` inverts the certified polynomial rate.
signature:
(epsilon K c : ℝ)
    (h_eps : 0 < epsilon) (hK : K ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0)
body: gradeCertifiedRisk (gradeCertifiedSampleSize epsilon K c) K c = epsilon
proof:
by
  unfold gradeCertifiedRisk gradeCertifiedSampleSize
  have hexp : (-(K / c)) * (-(c / K)) = 1 := by
    rw [neg_mul_neg, div_mul_div_comm, mul_comm c K, div_self (mul_ne_zero hK hc)]
  rw [← Real.rpow_mul (le_of_lt h_eps), hexp, Real.rpow_one]
raw:
theorem gradeCertifiedSampleSize_attains (epsilon K c : ℝ)
    (h_eps : 0 < epsilon) (hK : K ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    gradeCertifiedRisk (gradeCertifiedSampleSize epsilon K c) K c = epsilon := by
  unfold gradeCertifiedRisk gradeCertifiedSampleSize
  have hexp : (-(K / c)) * (-(c / K)) = 1 := by
    rw [neg_mul_neg, div_mul_div_comm, mul_comm c K, div_self (mul_ne_zero hK hc)]
  rw [← Real.rpow_mul (le_of_lt h_eps), hexp, Real.rpow_one]

name: gradeCertified_understates_sample_size
docstring:
**A grade-`K` sample-size calculation understates the requirement.**

    Stated with the crossing point as a hypothesis: wherever the power law sits
    below the exponential, the certificate's answer is short. The unconditional
    grade-one case is `twoPoint_understates_sample_size` below.
signature:
(epsilon K c : ℝ)
    (h_gap : epsilon ^ (-(K / c)) < Real.exp (1 / epsilon))
body: gradeCertifiedSampleSize epsilon K c < logRateSampleSize epsilon
proof:
by
  unfold gradeCertifiedSampleSize logRateSampleSize
  exact h_gap
raw:
theorem gradeCertified_understates_sample_size (epsilon K c : ℝ)
    (h_gap : epsilon ^ (-(K / c)) < Real.exp (1 / epsilon)) :
    gradeCertifiedSampleSize epsilon K c < logRateSampleSize epsilon := by
  unfold gradeCertifiedSampleSize logRateSampleSize
  exact h_gap

name: twoPoint_understates_sample_size
docstring:
**At a normalised grade one, the shortfall needs no crossing hypothesis.**

    What is unconditional here is the *crossing*: no hypothesis about where the
    two curves meet is needed, because `1/ε + 1 ≤ exp (1/ε)` holds everywhere.
    What is **not** unconditional is `h_grade : K/c ≤ 1`. That is a
    normalisation on the certificate constant `c`, and at `K = 1` it says
    exactly `c ≥ 1`; it is not automatic for a two-point argument, and it is
    stated as a hypothesis for that reason rather than folded into the prose.
    Under it, the certified sample size is at most `1/ε` while the requirement
    is `exp (1/ε)`, at every target accuracy in `(0, 1]`.

    For every grade, with no normalisation at all, see
    `gradeCertified_understates_sample_size_eventually` below, which gives the
    same conclusion once the target is sharp enough.
signature:
(epsilon K c : ℝ)
    (h_eps : 0 < epsilon) (h_eps_le : epsilon ≤ 1) (h_grade : K / c ≤ 1)
body: gradeCertifiedSampleSize epsilon K c < logRateSampleSize epsilon
proof:
by
  unfold gradeCertifiedSampleSize logRateSampleSize
  have h1 : epsilon ^ (-(K / c)) ≤ epsilon ^ (-(1 : ℝ)) :=
    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge h_eps h_eps_le (by linarith)
  have h2 : epsilon ^ (-(1 : ℝ)) = 1 / epsilon := by
    rw [Real.rpow_neg (le_of_lt h_eps), Real.rpow_one, one_div]
  have h3 : 1 / epsilon + 1 ≤ Real.exp (1 / epsilon) := Real.add_one_le_exp _
  rw [h2] at h1
  linarith
raw:
theorem twoPoint_understates_sample_size (epsilon K c : ℝ)
    (h_eps : 0 < epsilon) (h_eps_le : epsilon ≤ 1) (h_grade : K / c ≤ 1) :
    gradeCertifiedSampleSize epsilon K c < logRateSampleSize epsilon := by
  unfold gradeCertifiedSampleSize logRateSampleSize
  have h1 : epsilon ^ (-(K / c)) ≤ epsilon ^ (-(1 : ℝ)) :=
    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge h_eps h_eps_le (by linarith)
  have h2 : epsilon ^ (-(1 : ℝ)) = 1 / epsilon := by
    rw [Real.rpow_neg (le_of_lt h_eps), Real.rpow_one, one_div]
  have h3 : 1 / epsilon + 1 ≤ Real.exp (1 / epsilon) := Real.add_one_le_exp _
  rw [h2] at h1
  linarith

name: gradeCertified_understates_sample_size_eventually
docstring:
**Every grade understates, at no normalisation, once the target is sharp
    enough.**

    Written along the sharpening target `ε = 1/x` as `x → ∞`, which is where the
    statement has content and which keeps the filter on `atTop` rather than on a
    punctured neighbourhood of zero. At accuracy `1/x` the certified sample size
    is `x^(K/c)` and the requirement is `exp x`, so the claim is that a power is
    eventually beaten by the exponential — `isLittleO_rpow_exp_atTop`, which
    holds for every real exponent with no side condition. This is the general
    form of `twoPoint_understates_sample_size` with its normalisation `K/c ≤ 1`
    removed: no grade of certificate, however high, and no constant, however
    favourable, escapes the shortfall.
body:
∀ᶠ x : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
      gradeCertifiedSampleSize (1 / x) K c < logRateSampleSize (1 / x)
proof:
by
  have hbound := (isLittleO_rpow_exp_atTop (K / c)).bound
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2)
  filter_upwards [hbound, Filter.eventually_ge_atTop (2 : ℝ)] with x hx hx2
  have hx0 : (0 : ℝ) < x := by linarith
  have hxm : 0 < x ^ (K / c) := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hx0 (K / c)
  have hexp : 0 < Real.exp x := Real.exp_pos x
  have hle : x ^ (K / c) ≤ 1 / 2 * Real.exp x := by
    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (le_of_lt hxm), Real.norm_of_nonneg (le_of_lt hexp)] at hx
    exact hx
  have hcert : gradeCertifiedSampleSize (1 / x) K c = x ^ (K / c) := by
    unfold gradeCertifiedSampleSize
    rw [one_div, Real.inv_rpow (le_of_lt hx0), Real.rpow_neg (le_of_lt hx0), inv_inv]
  have hlog : logRateSampleSize (1 / x) = Real.exp x := by
    unfold logRateSampleSize
    rw [one_div_one_div]
  rw [hcert, hlog]
  linarith
raw:
theorem gradeCertified_understates_sample_size_eventually (K c : ℝ) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
      gradeCertifiedSampleSize (1 / x) K c < logRateSampleSize (1 / x) := by
  have hbound := (isLittleO_rpow_exp_atTop (K / c)).bound
    (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2)
  filter_upwards [hbound, Filter.eventually_ge_atTop (2 : ℝ)] with x hx hx2
  have hx0 : (0 : ℝ) < x := by linarith
  have hxm : 0 < x ^ (K / c) := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hx0 (K / c)
  have hexp : 0 < Real.exp x := Real.exp_pos x
  have hle : x ^ (K / c) ≤ 1 / 2 * Real.exp x := by
    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (le_of_lt hxm), Real.norm_of_nonneg (le_of_lt hexp)] at hx
    exact hx
  have hcert : gradeCertifiedSampleSize (1 / x) K c = x ^ (K / c) := by
    unfold gradeCertifiedSampleSize
    rw [one_div, Real.inv_rpow (le_of_lt hx0), Real.rpow_neg (le_of_lt hx0), inv_inv]
  have hlog : logRateSampleSize (1 / x) = Real.exp x := by
    unfold logRateSampleSize
    rw [one_div_one_div]
  rw [hcert, hlog]
  linarith

name: UnitProb
docstring: Unit interval as a subtype, used for Bernoulli probabilities.
raw: abbrev UnitProb := Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

name: bernoulliPMF
docstring: Bernoulli PMF on `Bool`, using mathlib's canonical construction.
raw:
noncomputable def bernoulliPMF (p : NNReal) (hp : p ≤ 1) : PMF Bool :=
  PMF.bernoulli p hp

name: bernoulliMeasure
docstring: Bernoulli probability measure induced by `bernoulliPMF`.
raw:
noncomputable def bernoulliMeasure (p : NNReal) (hp : p ≤ 1) : Measure Bool :=
  (bernoulliPMF p hp).toMeasure

name: bernoulliKL
docstring: KL divergence between Bernoulli laws, via `InformationTheory.klDiv`.
raw:
noncomputable def bernoulliKL (p q : NNReal) (hp : p ≤ 1) (hq : q ≤ 1) : ENNReal :=
  InformationTheory.klDiv (bernoulliMeasure p hp) (bernoulliMeasure q hq)

name: bernoulliKL_self
proof:
by
  simp [bernoulliKL, bernoulliMeasure, bernoulliPMF]
raw:
@[simp] theorem bernoulliKL_self (p : NNReal) (hp : p ≤ 1) :
    bernoulliKL p p hp hp = 0 := by
  simp [bernoulliKL, bernoulliMeasure, bernoulliPMF]

name: bernoulliKL_eq_zero_iff
signature:
(p q : NNReal) (hp : p ≤ 1) (hq : q ≤ 1)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (bernoulliMeasure p hp)] [IsFiniteMeasure (bernoulliMeasure q hq)]
body:
bernoulliKL p q hp hq = 0 ↔
      bernoulliMeasure p hp = bernoulliMeasure q hq
proof:
by
  simpa [bernoulliKL] using
    (InformationTheory.klDiv_eq_zero_iff
      (μ := bernoulliMeasure p hp) (ν := bernoulliMeasure q hq))
raw:
theorem bernoulliKL_eq_zero_iff (p q : NNReal) (hp : p ≤ 1) (hq : q ≤ 1)
    [IsFiniteMeasure (bernoulliMeasure p hp)] [IsFiniteMeasure (bernoulliMeasure q hq)] :
    bernoulliKL p q hp hq = 0 ↔
      bernoulliMeasure p hp = bernoulliMeasure q hq := by
  simpa [bernoulliKL] using
    (InformationTheory.klDiv_eq_zero_iff
      (μ := bernoulliMeasure p hp) (ν := bernoulliMeasure q hq))

name: unitProbToNNReal
docstring: Coercion helper from `[0,1]` real probabilities to `NNReal`.

name: unitProbToNNReal_le_one
proof:

  exact p.2.2

name: klBern

name: stdGaussianMeasure
docstring: The standard Gaussian measure μ = N(0,1).
raw: noncomputable def stdGaussianMeasure : MeasureTheory.Measure Real := ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1

name: poly_n
docstring: Polynomial function x^n.
raw: def poly_n (n : Nat) (x : Real) : Real := x ^ n

name: integrable_poly_n
docstring:
For any natural number n, x^n is integrable with respect to the standard Gaussian measure.
    This follows from the finiteness of Gaussian moments.
proof:
by
  have h_gauss_integral : ∀ n : ℕ, MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => x^n * Real.exp (-x^2 / 2)) (Set.univ : Set ℝ) := by
    intro n
    have := @integrable_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq
    simpa [ div_eq_inv_mul ] using @this ( 1 / 2 ) ( by norm_num ) n ( by linarith )
  unfold poly_n
  unfold stdGaussianMeasure
  simp_all +decide [ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal]
  refine' MeasureTheory.Integrable.mono' _ _ _
  refine' fun x => |x ^ n|
  · refine' MeasureTheory.Integrable.abs _
    rw [ MeasureTheory.integrable_withDensity_iff ]
    · convert h_gauss_integral n |> fun h => h.div_const ( Real.sqrt ( 2 * Real.pi ) ) using 2 ; norm_num [ ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDF ] ; ring
      norm_num [ ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDFReal ] ; ring
      rw [ ENNReal.toReal_ofReal ( Real.exp_nonneg _ ) ]
    · fun_prop
    · simp [ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDF]
  · exact Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable ( by continuity )
  · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => Real.norm_eq_abs _ ▸ le_rfl
raw:
theorem integrable_poly_n (n : Nat) : MeasureTheory.Integrable (poly_n n) stdGaussianMeasure := by
  have h_gauss_integral : ∀ n : ℕ, MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => x^n * Real.exp (-x^2 / 2)) (Set.univ : Set ℝ) := by
    intro n
    have := @integrable_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq
    simpa [ div_eq_inv_mul ] using @this ( 1 / 2 ) ( by norm_num ) n ( by linarith )
  unfold poly_n
  unfold stdGaussianMeasure
  simp_all +decide [ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal]
  refine' MeasureTheory.Integrable.mono' _ _ _
  refine' fun x => |x ^ n|
  · refine' MeasureTheory.Integrable.abs _
    rw [ MeasureTheory.integrable_withDensity_iff ]
    · convert h_gauss_integral n |> fun h => h.div_const ( Real.sqrt ( 2 * Real.pi ) ) using 2 ; norm_num [ ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDF ] ; ring
      norm_num [ ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDFReal ] ; ring
      rw [ ENNReal.toReal_ofReal ( Real.exp_nonneg _ ) ]
    · fun_prop
    · simp [ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDF]
  · exact Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable ( by continuity )
  · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => Real.norm_eq_abs _ ▸ le_rfl

name: integrable_sq_gaussian
docstring: x^2 is integrable with respect to the standard Gaussian measure.
proof:
by
  apply integrable_poly_n 2
raw:
theorem integrable_sq_gaussian : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => x ^ 2) stdGaussianMeasure := by
  apply integrable_poly_n 2

name: integrable_id_gaussian
docstring: x is integrable with respect to the standard Gaussian measure.
proof:
by
  have h := integrable_poly_n 1
  unfold poly_n at h
  simp only [pow_one] at h
  exact h
raw:
theorem integrable_id_gaussian : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => x) stdGaussianMeasure := by
  have h := integrable_poly_n 1
  unfold poly_n at h
  simp only [pow_one] at h
  exact h

name: integrable_pow4_gaussian
docstring: x^4 is integrable with respect to the standard Gaussian measure (useful for variance calculations).
proof:
by
  apply integrable_poly_n 4
raw:
theorem integrable_pow4_gaussian : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => x ^ 4) stdGaussianMeasure := by
  apply integrable_poly_n 4

name: integrable_prod_mul
docstring:
If f is integrable on μ and g is integrable on ν, then f(x) * g(y) is integrable on μ.prod ν.
    This is essential for Fubini-type arguments on product measures.
signature:
{X Y : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y]
    {μ : Measure X} {ν : Measure Y} [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν]
    (f : X → ℝ) (g : Y → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) (hg : Integrable g ν)

name: HardyWeinbergModel.genotypeProb_sum
docstring: Hardy-Weinberg genotype probabilities sum to `1`.
proof:
by
  have hsum : h.refFreq + h.altFreq = 1 := by
    unfold HardyWeinbergModel.refFreq
    ring
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ g : DiploidGenotype, h.genotypeProb g) =
        ∑ i : Fin 3, h.genotypeProb (DiploidGenotype.equivFin3.symm i) := by
    exact Fintype.sum_equiv DiploidGenotype.equivFin3 _ _ (by
      intro x
      rw [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3_symm_apply_apply])
  rw [hrewrite]
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3, HardyWeinbergModel.genotypeProb]
  calc
    h.refFreq ^ 2 + 2 * h.refFreq * h.altFreq + h.altFreq ^ 2
        = (h.refFreq + h.altFreq) ^ 2 := by ring
    _ = 1 := by rw [hsum]; norm_num
raw:

    (∑ g : DiploidGenotype, h.genotypeProb g) = 1 := by
  have hsum : h.refFreq + h.altFreq = 1 := by
    unfold HardyWeinbergModel.refFreq
    ring
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ g : DiploidGenotype, h.genotypeProb g) =
        ∑ i : Fin 3, h.genotypeProb (DiploidGenotype.equivFin3.symm i) := by
    exact Fintype.sum_equiv DiploidGenotype.equivFin3 _ _ (by
      intro x
      rw [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3_symm_apply_apply])
  rw [hrewrite]
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3, HardyWeinbergModel.genotypeProb]
  calc
    h.refFreq ^ 2 + 2 * h.refFreq * h.altFreq + h.altFreq ^ 2
        = (h.refFreq + h.altFreq) ^ 2 := by ring
    _ = 1 := by rw [hsum]; norm_num

name: HardyWeinbergModel.expectedAltAlleleCount
docstring:
Expected alternative-allele count under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

    Empirical status: UNTESTED.
body: ∑ g : DiploidGenotype, altAlleleCount g * h.genotypeProb g
raw:

  ∑ g : DiploidGenotype, altAlleleCount g * h.genotypeProb g

name: HardyWeinbergModel.expectedAltAlleleCount_eq
proof:
by
  have hsum : h.refFreq + h.altFreq = 1 := by
    unfold HardyWeinbergModel.refFreq
    ring
  unfold HardyWeinbergModel.expectedAltAlleleCount
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ g : DiploidGenotype, altAlleleCount g * h.genotypeProb g) =
        ∑ i : Fin 3, altAlleleCount (DiploidGenotype.equivFin3.symm i) *
          h.genotypeProb (DiploidGenotype.equivFin3.symm i) := by
    exact Fintype.sum_equiv DiploidGenotype.equivFin3 _ _ (by
      intro x
      rw [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3_symm_apply_apply])
  rw [hrewrite]
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3, HardyWeinbergModel.genotypeProb]
  calc
    altAlleleCount DiploidGenotype.homRef * h.refFreq ^ 2 +
        altAlleleCount DiploidGenotype.het * (2 * h.refFreq * h.altFreq) +
        altAlleleCount DiploidGenotype.homAlt * h.altFreq ^ 2
        = 2 * (h.refFreq * h.altFreq) + 2 * h.altFreq ^ 2 := by
          simp [altAlleleCount]
          ring
    _ 
        = 2 * h.altFreq * (h.refFreq + h.altFreq) := by ring
    _ = 2 * h.altFreq := by rw [hsum]; ring
raw:

    (h : HardyWeinbergModel) :
    h.expectedAltAlleleCount = 2 * h.altFreq := by
  have hsum : h.refFreq + h.altFreq = 1 := by
    unfold HardyWeinbergModel.refFreq
    ring
  unfold HardyWeinbergModel.expectedAltAlleleCount
  have hrewrite :
      (∑ g : DiploidGenotype, altAlleleCount g * h.genotypeProb g) =
        ∑ i : Fin 3, altAlleleCount (DiploidGenotype.equivFin3.symm i) *
          h.genotypeProb (DiploidGenotype.equivFin3.symm i) := by
    exact Fintype.sum_equiv DiploidGenotype.equivFin3 _ _ (by
      intro x
      rw [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3_symm_apply_apply])
  rw [hrewrite]
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp [DiploidGenotype.equivFin3, HardyWeinbergModel.genotypeProb]
  calc
    altAlleleCount DiploidGenotype.homRef * h.refFreq ^ 2 +
        altAlleleCount DiploidGenotype.het * (2 * h.refFreq * h.altFreq) +
        altAlleleCount DiploidGenotype.homAlt * h.altFreq ^ 2
        = 2 * (h.refFreq * h.altFreq) + 2 * h.altFreq ^ 2 := by
          simp [altAlleleCount]
          ring
    _ 
        = 2 * h.altFreq * (h.refFreq + h.altFreq) := by ring
    _ = 2 * h.altFreq := by rw [hsum]; ring

docstring:

We write the denominator as `σ² * sqrt(σ²)` to stay inside the existing real-analysis library.

  unfold berryEsseenErrorBound
  by_cases hzero : variance * Real.sqrt variance = 0
  · simp [hzero]

name: tail_probability_error_of_cdf_error
docstring:
If a score CDF is within `ε` of an approximating CDF at threshold `t`,
then the corresponding tail probability is also within `ε`.
proof:
by
  have h := cert.pointwise_error t
  calc
    |((1 - cert.exactCdf t) - (1 - cert.approxCdf t))|
        = |-(cert.exactCdf t - cert.approxCdf t)| := by ring_nf
    _ = |cert.exactCdf t - cert.approxCdf t| := by rw [abs_neg]
    _ ≤ cert.epsilon := h
raw:
theorem tail_probability_error_of_cdf_error
    (cert : CdfApproximationCertificate) (t : ℝ) :
    |((1 - cert.exactCdf t) - (1 - cert.approxCdf t))| ≤ cert.epsilon := by
  have h := cert.pointwise_error t
  calc
    |((1 - cert.exactCdf t) - (1 - cert.approxCdf t))|
        = |-(cert.exactCdf t - cert.approxCdf t)| := by ring_nf
    _ = |cert.exactCdf t - cert.approxCdf t| := by rw [abs_neg]
    _ ≤ cert.epsilon := h

signature:

name: noise_integrated_cdf
docstring:
Integrating out Gaussian environmental noise gives a Gaussian CDF at threshold `t`:
`P(μ + E ≤ t | x) = CDF_{N(μ,σ²(x))}(t)`.
signature:
{k : ℕ} (hN : GaussianNoiseAssumption k)
    (x : Fin k → ℝ) (μ t : ℝ)
body:
noiseMeasureGivenX hN x {e : ℝ | μ + e ≤ t} =
      ENNReal.ofReal (ProbabilityTheory.cdf
        (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal μ (hN.sigma2 x)) t)
proof:
by
  calc
    noiseMeasureGivenX hN x {e : ℝ | μ + e ≤ t}
        = ((noiseMeasureGivenX hN x).map (fun e : ℝ => μ + e)) (Set.Iic t) := by
            rw [Measure.map_apply (by fun_prop) measurableSet_Iic]
            rfl
    _ = (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal μ (hN.sigma2 x)) (Set.Iic t) := by
          simp [noiseMeasureGivenX, ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal_map_const_add]

name: liability_threshold_probit_raw
docstring:
Exact threshold-event probability after integrating Gaussian environmental noise:
`P(Y=1 | S=s, x) = 1 - P(L ≤ T(x) | S=s, x)`.
signature:
{k : ℕ} (hN : GaussianNoiseAssumption k)
    (T : (Fin k → ℝ) → ℝ) (x : Fin k → ℝ) (s : ℝ)
body:
noiseMeasureGivenX hN x (diseaseEvent T x s) =
      1 - ENNReal.ofReal (ProbabilityTheory.cdf
        (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal s (hN.sigma2 x)) (T x))
proof:
by
  have h_le :
      noiseMeasureGivenX hN x {e : ℝ | latentLiability s e ≤ T x} =
        ENNReal.ofReal (ProbabilityTheory.cdf
          (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal s (hN.sigma2 x)) (T x)) := by
    simpa [latentLiability] using noise_integrated_cdf hN x s (T x)
  have h_le_set :
      ({e : ℝ | latentLiability s e ≤ T x} : Set ℝ) = Set.Iic (T x - s) := by
    ext e
    constructor
    · intro h
      change e ≤ T x - s
      have hsle : latentLiability s e ≤ T x := by simpa using h
      dsimp [latentLiability] at hsle
      linarith
    · intro h
      change latentLiability s e ≤ T x
      have hle : e ≤ T x - s := by simpa [Set.mem_Iic] using h
      dsimp [latentLiability]
      linarith
  have h_event :
      diseaseEvent T x s = (Set.Iic (T x - s))ᶜ := by
    ext e
    constructor
    · intro h
      change ¬ e ≤ T x - s
      intro hle
      have hsle : s + e ≤ T x := by linarith
      exact (not_le_of_gt h) hsle
    · intro h
      change s + e > T x
      by_contra hnot
      have hsle : s + e ≤ T x := le_of_not_gt hnot
      have hle : e ≤ T x - s := by linarith
      exact h hle
  have h_meas_le : MeasurableSet (Set.Iic (T x - s) : Set ℝ) := measurableSet_Iic
  have h_le' :
      noiseMeasureGivenX hN x (Set.Iic (T x - s)) =
        ENNReal.ofReal (ProbabilityTheory.cdf
          (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal s (hN.sigma2 x)) (T x)) := by
    simpa [h_le_set] using h_le
  rw [h_event]
  rw [measure_compl (s := (Set.Iic (T x - s) : Set ℝ)) h_meas_le
    (measure_ne_top (noiseMeasureGivenX hN x) _)]
  rw [measure_univ, h_le']

name: liability_threshold_probit_real
docstring:
Real-valued form of the liability-threshold probability:
`P(Y=1 | S=s, x) = 1 - CDF_{N(s,σ²(x))}(T(x))`.
signature:
{k : ℕ} (hN : GaussianNoiseAssumption k)
    (T : (Fin k → ℝ) → ℝ) (x : Fin k → ℝ) (s : ℝ)

    exact_mod_cast
      (ProbabilityTheory.cdf_le_one
        (μ := ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal s (hN.sigma2 x)) (T x))
  rw [ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le h_le (by simp)]
  simp [ProbabilityTheory.cdf_nonneg]

name: independent_product_mean_zero
docstring:
E[P · C_l] = 0 when P and C are independent standard normals.
    This is the key fact that eliminates cross-terms in risk calculations.
proof:
by
  let μP : Measure ℝ := ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1
  let μC : Measure (Fin k → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi (fun (_ : Fin k) => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
  have hPC :
      ∫ pc, pc.1 * pc.2 l ∂(μP.prod μC) =
        (∫ p, p ∂μP) * (∫ c, c l ∂μC) := by
    simpa using
      (MeasureTheory.integral_prod_mul (μ := μP) (ν := μC)
        (f := fun p : ℝ => p) (g := fun c : Fin k → ℝ => c l))
  have hC_map : μC.map (Function.eval l) = ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1 := by
    simpa [μC] using
      (MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_eval
        (μ := fun (_ : Fin k) => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) l).map_eq
  have h_eval_ae : AEMeasurable (Function.eval l) μC := by
    exact
      (MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_eval
        (μ := fun (_ : Fin k) => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) l).measurable.aemeasurable
  have hC0 : (∫ c, c l ∂μC) = 0 := by
    calc
      ∫ c, c l ∂μC = ∫ x, x ∂(μC.map (Function.eval l)) := by
        simpa using
          (MeasureTheory.integral_map (μ := μC) (φ := Function.eval l)
            (f := fun x : ℝ => x) h_eval_ae aestronglyMeasurable_id).symm
      _ = ∫ x, x ∂(ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) := by rw [hC_map]
      _ = 0 := gaussian_mean_zero
  have h_prod : stdNormalProdMeasure k = μP.prod μC := by
    simp [stdNormalProdMeasure, μP, μC]
  calc
    ∫ pc, pc.1 * pc.2 l ∂(stdNormalProdMeasure k)
        = ∫ pc, pc.1 * pc.2 l ∂(μP.prod μC) := by rw [h_prod]
    _ = (∫ p, p ∂μP) * (∫ c, c l ∂μC) := hPC
    _ = 0 := by simp [hC0]

    (densityRatio : Ω → ℝ) (X : Ω → ι → ℝ)
    (residual : Ω → ℝ) : ι → ℝ :=
  rawCrossMoment P X (fun ω => (densityRatio ω - 1) * residual ω)

name: dot_weightedResidualMoment
docstring:
Pairing the shifted residual moment with a direction is exactly the scalar
`L²` pairing to which Cauchy--Schwarz applies.
signature:
(P : ExpFunctional Ω) (densityRatio : Ω → ℝ)
    (X : Ω → ι → ℝ) (residual : Ω → ℝ) (direction : ι → ℝ)
body:
dot direction (weightedResidualMoment P densityRatio X residual) =
      P (fun ω =>
        (densityRatio ω - 1) * (dot direction (X ω) * residual ω))
proof:
by
  unfold weightedResidualMoment rawCrossMoment dot
  have hexpand :
      (fun ω =>
        (densityRatio ω - 1) *
          ((∑ i, direction i * X ω i) * residual ω)) =
        ∑ i, (direction i) •
          (fun ω => X ω i * ((densityRatio ω - 1) * residual ω)) := by
    funext ω
    calc
      (densityRatio ω - 1) *
          ((∑ i, direction i * X ω i) * residual ω) =
          ((densityRatio ω - 1) * residual ω) *
            ∑ i, direction i * X ω i := by ring
      _ = ∑ i, ((densityRatio ω - 1) * residual ω) *
            (direction i * X ω i) := by rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      _ = ∑ i, (direction i) •
            (fun ω => X ω i * ((densityRatio ω - 1) * residual ω)) ω := by
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro i _
          simp only [smul_eq_mul]
          ring
      _ = (∑ i, (direction i) •
            (fun ω => X ω i * ((densityRatio ω - 1) * residual ω))) ω := by
          simp only [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply]
  rw [hexpand, ExpFunctional.eval_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [P.smul_eval]

name: weighted_residual_moment_directional_bound
docstring:
Directional chi-square bound.  This is the exact product of distributional
discrepancy and residual nonlinearity before optimizing over directions.
signature:
(P : ExpFunctional Ω) (densityRatio : Ω → ℝ)
    (X : Ω → ι → ℝ) (residual : Ω → ℝ) (direction : ι → ℝ)
    (hCauchySchwarz : ∀ f g : Ω → ℝ,
      P (fun ω => f ω * g ω) ^ 2 ≤
        P (fun ω => f ω ^ 2) * P (fun ω => g ω ^ 2))
body:
dot direction (weightedResidualMoment P densityRatio X residual) ^ 2 ≤
      chiSquareBudget P densityRatio *
        directionalResidualCurvature P X residual direction
proof:
by
  rw [dot_weightedResidualMoment]
  exact hCauchySchwarz
    (fun ω => densityRatio ω - 1)
    (fun ω => dot direction (X ω) * residual ω)
binders:
∀ f g : Ω → ℝ,
      P (fun ω => f ω * g ω) ^ 2 ≤
        P (fun ω => f ω ^ 2) * P (fun ω => g ω ^ 2)

    (P : ExpFunctional Ω) (densityRatio : Ω → ℝ)
    (X : Ω → ι → ℝ) (residual : Ω → ℝ) (direction : ι → ℝ)
    (hCauchySchwarz : ∀ f g : Ω → ℝ,
      P (fun ω => f ω * g ω) ^ 2 ≤
        P (fun ω => f ω ^ 2) * P (fun ω => g ω ^ 2)) :
    dot direction (weightedResidualMoment P densityRatio X residual) ^ 2 ≤
      chiSquareBudget P densityRatio *
